title: The Stealth Tax Destroying Housing Affordability — TikTok
notes: Story follows the article's arc: premiums outrun rent → the map → the share of a mortgage → property taxes → New York's subsidy math → insurers pay out less (loss ratio, denied claims, jets, record premiums) → renters pay → hold insurers accountable.
All figures are from the article (Sep 9, 2026) and the sources it cites (NBER, NAIC, Vanderbilt Policy Accelerator, NYC EDC).
The author's edits run past the usual 89s cap; allowed for this video (max_seconds 105).

post.headline: The stealth tax making housing unaffordable
post.caption: Home insurance premiums rose 71% since 2018, more than twice as fast as rent. Insurers blame climate, but the share of premiums they pay back in claims fell from 80% to 55%. Renters end up paying the difference.
post.cta: Full story and interactive maps at the link in bio.

headline.text: Home insurance premiums are up {71%} since 2018.

say: Home insurance premiums have risen 71% since 2018.

scenes.title: Increase since 2018
say: Rent rose 30% over the same years, so insurance climbed more than twice as fast.
Our recent article uncovered that insurance premiums and property taxes have become a stealth tax draining household budgets.
Premiums are highest along the Gulf Coast and in Florida, where a typical policy can top $5,000 a year.

scenes.title: Home insurance, as a share of a monthly mortgage
scenes.source: The Stealth Tax Destroying Housing Affordability · American Inequality
say: Home insurance now makes up more than 10% of a monthly mortgage, up from 5% twenty years ago.

overlays.label: extra in property taxes each year

scenes.source: The Stealth Tax Destroying Housing Affordability · American Inequality
say: Property tax bills are rising faster than inflation, costing the average American an extra $4,500 a year.
In New York City, every $100 increase in insurance costs requires $1,200 more in city subsidies to keep public housing affordable.

scenes.title: Share of premiums paid back in claims
scenes.subtitle: the loss ratio
say: Insurers blame climate, but the share of premiums they pay back in claims fell from a historical average of 80% to just 55%.

scenes.title: Claims resolved last year by the 5 biggest home insurers
scenes.source: The Stealth Tax Destroying Housing Affordability · American Inequality
say: Meanwhile, they are raking in record profits. The 5 biggest home insurers didn't pay out on 44% of the claims they resolved last year.
When they were telling states that climate change was making their business unaffordable, the top 10 property insurers bought 16 private jets.

overlays.label: in premiums last year, more than the U.S. military budget

scenes.source: NAIC · The Stealth Tax Destroying Housing Affordability
say: Those companies took in $1.03 trillion in premiums last year, more than the entire U.S. military budget.
But insurers aren't only to blame. Landlords often pass these costs on to renters or force the city to pick up the bill through vouchers.

scenes.text: Hold insurers accountable to {the neighborhoods they leave exposed.}
say: Communities need to bring these invisible costs under control and hold insurers accountable to the neighborhoods they leave exposed.
You can read the full story on American Inequality.
